name: Umweltbonus (original)
notes: Federal share + equal manufacturer share. BEV list price up to 60k EUR.

name: Umweltbonus raised
notes: Announced at the Autogipfel on 4 Nov 2019. Guideline in force 19 Feb 2020 after EU approval, retroactive for cars registered after 4 Nov 2019 (official FAQ says 5 Nov). Amounts for net list price up to 40k EUR.

name: Innovationspraemie (federal share doubled)
notes: Konjunkturpaket of 3 Jun 2020. Guideline published 7 Jul and in force 8 Jul 2020, retroactive for cars registered after 3 Jun 2020. Originally limited to 31 Dec 2021. Amounts for net list price up to 40k EUR.

name: Innovationspraemie extended to 2022
notes: Same amounts as R2. Announced by BMWK on 13 Dec 2021, in force 1 Jan 2022.

name: Umweltbonus 2023 (reduced; PHEV excluded)
notes: BMWK press release 26 Jul 2022. BEV federal share 4500 EUR up to 40k list price (3000 EUR for 40-65k). PHEV support ended 31 Dec 2022. Manufacturer share assumed to be half of the federal share (2250 EUR): check against the 2023 guideline.

name: Umweltbonus private buyers only
notes: Same press release as R3: from 1 Sep 2023 companies are no longer eligible. Amounts for a private BEV buyer unchanged.

name: Umweltbonus stopped
notes: Decided 13 Dec 2023 in the KTF budget talks, announced by BMWK on Saturday 16 Dec 2023. No new applications from 18 Dec 2023 00:00. It had been planned to run until end of 2024.

name: E-Auto-Foerderung 2026 (income based)
notes: Coalition committee agreement 9 Oct 2025; details presented 19 Jan 2026; portal opened 19 May 2026; retroactive for first registrations from 1 Jan 2026. No manufacturer share. BEV 3000 base + up to 2000 income supplement + up to 1000 child supplement (max 6000). PHEV/EREV 1500 base, max 4500, only if <=60 g CO2/km and >=80 km electric range, registrations until 30 Jun 2027. Household taxable income cap 80k EUR (up to 90k with children). Budget 3 bn EUR.
